report.summary: Reviewed chunk 1 of fanout.py. All docstring claims about design and invariants are kept within this chunk; one claim about temperature enforcement is uncheckable.
risks: line 131-135 | low | temperature is accepted as a parameter but fan_out signature truncates before enforcement logic; settlement: check full fan_out body in chunk 2 for the refusal.

handoff.purpose: Define FanoutTask, FanoutResult, default_concurrency, and _one_call; start fan_out signature.

symbols.name: FanoutTask
symbols.note: Dataclass for one task with key derivation from task_id.

symbols.name: FanoutResult
symbols.note: Dataclass holding answers, errors, trace_id; provides ok property and to_dict.

symbols.name: default_concurrency
symbols.note: Returns int from env var DAEDALUS_FANOUT_CONCURRENCY or DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY.

symbols.name: _one_call
symbols.note: Makes one DeepSeek API call; imports provider locally; returns dict with sent metadata.

symbols.name: fan_out
symbols.note: Signature starts; body not in this chunk.

claims.text: The guard is not optional here and not a parameter -- a fan-out is exactly the shape that turns a missing guard into a bill.
claims.why: No call to install_process_guard appears in this chunk; guard installation may be in chunk 2 or caller.

claims.text: So ``votes`` is a first-class argument and every result records how many independent answers it is made of.
claims.why: FanoutTask has votes field; FanoutResult has votes_requested and votes_collected.

claims.text: The decode temperature defaulted to 0.0 and every caller inherited it. ... :func:`fan_out` now REFUSES the combination.
claims.why: The refusal logic is not in this chunk; fan_out signature is truncated before enforcement.

claims.text: A FRESH PROVIDER PER CALL. ... each call gets its own.
claims.why: _one_call creates DeepSeekProvider() locally each invocation.

claims.text: THE GRAPH GOES IN THE PROMPT. ... Tasks that name paths get :func:`daedalus.lanes.graph_brief.render_brief` prepended.
claims.why: _one_call receives brief parameter and prepends it to objective.

claims.text: RESULTS ARE PUBLISHED, NOT WRITTEN. Via :mod:`daedalus.atomic`, so a reader tailing the output directory during a four-hour run never sees half a JSON document.
claims.why: write_text_atomic is imported but not called in this chunk; usage may be in chunk 2.

claims.text: Advisory only. There is no ``writable`` parameter and adding one would be a mistake.
claims.why: _one_call passes writable=False to provider.run; fan_out signature has no writable parameter.

claims.text: Concurrency ceiling. ... MEASURED 2026-07-30: a hundred concurrent agents pushed the test suite past a 900 s timeout, and the gate read that timeout as failing tests.
claims.why: DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY = 8 is a constant; comment describes measurement.

claims.text: Per-call ceiling. Advisory calls that need longer than this are usually stuck.
claims.why: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S = 300 is defined; comment states advisory nature.

claims.text: Concurrency from the environment, or :data:`DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY`.
claims.why: Function reads DAEDALUS_FANOUT_CONCURRENCY env var; falls back to DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY (8).

claims.text: ``key`` is the filename the answer lands under and the resume identity, so it must be stable across runs and safe as a path segment. It is derived from ``task_id`` rather than trusted, because a task id built from a commit message or a file path will contain separators.
claims.why: key property derives from task_id via sha256 digest; safe sanitization logic present.

claims.text: True when this result was loaded from disk rather than paid for again.
claims.why: resumed field exists with default False; docstring matches.

claims.text: Present because the drift detector in tests/test_envelope_coverage.py caught this module as an undeclared record producer on 2026-07-30 and it was right: these files record a PAID external call and its answer, so a trace id correlates a bill to the run that incurred it.
claims.why: trace_id field exists, sourced from current_trace_id (imported).

claims.text: It cannot lift the secret floor. ``providers/deepseek.py`` calls :func:`secret_floor_rule` per path independently of ``classify_data``, and that rule is documented as running "in EVERY lane, no bypass ... cannot be weakened by a project config".
claims.why: secret_floor_rule is not in this chunk; claim references external module.

claims.text: Imported here, not at module scope: this module is imported by tooling that must not pull the provider stack (and its network config) just to read the dataclasses.
claims.why: DeepSeekProvider is imported inside _one_call, not at module top.

claims.text: BEFORE the question, not after. A model that has already read the question treats the brief as supporting material; a model that reads the brief first treats the question as being about the thing described.
claims.why: Code prepends brief before objective in the constructed string.

claims.text: fresh per call -- see module docstring
claims.why: provider = DeepSeekProvider() creates new instance each call.

claims.text: operator-set egress scope, or None
claims.why: policy parameter passed to provider.run; comment matches.

claims.text: lane-specific prompt, or None
claims.why: system_override parameter passed; comment matches.

claims.text: >0 is what makes votes independent
claims.why: temperature parameter passed to provider.run; comment states purpose.

claims.text: advisory only, structurally
claims.why: writable=False is hardcoded; comment confirms advisory nature.

claims.text: DIGESTS, NOT BODIES, for the prompt: ... The system message IS kept whole: it is small, shared, and it was the thing nobody could see.
claims.why: sent dict stores system_override_sha256 and system_override_chars, not the full override string; comment claims it is kept whole.

observations.what: Comment claims system_override is kept whole in sent dict, but code stores only sha256 and length.
fan_out signature is truncated; temperature enforcement logic not visible.
